Prevention: Try to avoid growing new tomato crops near older crops as the inoculum will spread.
Use correct spacing ranging from 60-75 x 60-90cm.
If purchasing plants, buy certified seedlings.
Powdery mildews are unusual in that they like dry conditions.
Spraying the crop with water will deter powdery mildew, but may encourage other diseases.
This can be important under greenhouse conditions.
Avoid growing near other susceptible crops (pepper and cotton especially).
Monitoring: Scout weekly and look out for:
White powdery growth on the upper leaf surface
Take action as soon as symptoms are seen on one plant, if early in the season.
More mature crops may not need control.
Direct Control: If early in the season and the infection has just started, rub the colonies off the leaf with your thumb.
If the infection is spreading and the crop is far from mature, chemical sprays may be required.
Mix 1 tablespoon potassium bicarbonate and ½ teaspoon liquid soap (not detergent) in 1 gallon of water.
Spray with thiophanate- methyl based products.
Spray with carbendazim- based products. 750 ml in 1000L water per hectare (for 500g/L concentrate)
Fluopyram +Trifloxystrobin based products at recommended rates.
Restrictions: Follow instructions on the product label, e.g. dosage, max. number of applications, PHI, REI, proper pesticide waste disposal, among others.
Registered pesticides www.pcpb.go.ke 50 grams of product (80% sulphur) per 20L knapsack spray tank.
20mls of concentrate per 20L knapsack sprayer (if the concentrate is 400g/litre).
PHI is 3 days, only one applcation per season.
